question:
A 45-year-old male from the midwest seeks medical attention due to one week of painless hematuria,
accompanied by fatigue and lethargy. He reports a 9.0 kg weight loss over six months. His social
history includes occasional weekend beer consumption (1-2 beers) for the past decade, with no
smoking history. His occupational history reveals 30 years of employment at a plastic chemical plant,
and he has never traveled internationally. Family history is significant for a father who died of a heart
attack at 62 and a distant relative with pancreatic cancer. Physical examination is unremarkable with
stable vital signs. Urinalysis confirms the presence of RBCs. A cystoscopy reveals a pedunculated
mass extending into the bladder lumen, with biopsy confirming malignancy. Which of the following
represents the most concerning risk factor for this patient's condition? Answer Choices: (A) Chronic
urinary tract infections (B) Vinyl chloride exposure (C) Exposure to ionizing radiation (D) Aromatic
amine exposure (E) *Schistosoma haematobium* infection (F) Chronic alcohol consumption (G)
Benzene exposure (H) Long-term NSAID use (I) Family history of pancreatic cancer (J) Occupational
asbestos exposure
 A. *Schistosoma haematobium* infection
B. Family history of pancreatic cancer
C. Exposure to ionizing radiation
D. Long-term NSAID use
E. Chronic urinary tract infections
F. Occupational asbestos exposure
G. Chronic alcohol consumption
H. Benzene exposure
I. Aromatic amine exposure
J. Vinyl chloride exposure
